items.h: Michael Penix Jr. Is a Streamer Riding a Touchdown Run
items.s: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is a streamer worth adding in leagues with at least 14 teams ahead of Week 8 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, then the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 9. He followed his three-touchdown performance against the Chicago Bears with another three scores in Sunday's 29-20 victory over the San Francisco 49ers, despite throwing for just 213 yards. Penix completed 25 of 34 passes without an interception, connecting with Nick Muse, Kyle Pitts, and Drake London for touchdowns. He also avoided a sack after being brought down five times against the Bears in Week 6. The 26-year-old has thrown six touchdowns without an interception over his past two starts,…

items.h: Week 7 winners and losers: Pollard, Burrow lead the way; Walker III, Purdy struggle
items.s: Tony Pollard, Joe Burrow and Zay Flowers came up big in Week 7, while Brock Purdy, Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker III all had quiet days.

items.h: Three TDs in Week 7 win
items.s: Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added five carries for minus-1 yard in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble. Penix put together a solid, mistake-free effort that saw him toss a trio of touchdown passes for the second straight game. items.h: Michael Penix Jr. has Efficient Day to Give 49ers Their First Loss
items.s: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. led his team to an upset victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers. Penix had a productive and efficient day against the 49ers, as he completed 25 out of 34 passing attempts (73.5%) for 213 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. In fact, the Falcons didn't turn the ball over at all, while the 49ers gave the ball away four times, which obviously played a big role for the Falcons in their win. On Sunday, Penix connected on touchdown passes with wide receiver Drake London, tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. and tight end Nick Muse. Penix has now had back-to-back games in which he has thrown for at least 213 yards, three touchdowns…

items.h: Michael Penix Jr. tosses three touchdowns in win over 49ers
items.s: Michael Penix Jr. completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 29-20 win over the 49ers. Penix made himself quite comfortable in this impressive performance, avoiding any sacks and committing no turnovers. Penix had just one three-touchdown game in his career before last week. He has now thrown three in each of the last two games without an interception. The 26-year-old QB has settled in at the helm of the Falcons' offense and is climbing the fantasy ranks.

items.h: Michael Penix Jr. a Low-End QB2 Against Stout 49ers Defense
items.s: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw for 225 yards and a season-high three touchdowns with no interceptions in last week's loss to the Bears. He was able to put up those numbers despite completing a season-low 57.6 percent of his passes (19-for-33). That makes back-to-back weeks with sub-60 percent completion rates, and Week 7 brings another tough matchup against the 49ers, who feature Raheem Morris at defensive coordinator, the same person who drafted Penix back in 2024 while serving as the head coach in Atlanta, so he's quite familiar with the left-handed quarterback. The former first-rounder was sacked five times last week, the most he's been sacked in the four games he's…

items.h: Michael Penix Jr. a Waiver Priority in Two-QB Leagues After Three-TD Game
items.s: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. had his most fantasy-friendly day in Sunday's Week 6 loss to the Chicago Bears, as he completed 19 of his season-high 33 pass attempts for 225 yards and three touchdowns. Penix did not throw an interception for the third straight game, and he now has at least one touchdown pass in his four starts in 2026. Down 28-7 going into the fourth quarter in Atlanta, Penix made things interesting late in the game, and the Falcons only lost by one score (eight points). He effectively spread the ball around to all of his weapons, including Drake London, Jahan Dotson, rookie Zachariah Branch, and tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. Through four games in his third year…

items.h: Michael Penix Jr. Looks Sharp in Loss
items.s: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. put together a strong performance under center during Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears. He completed 19-of-33 passing attempts for 225 yards with three touchdowns and zero interceptions in the loss. Penix was mostly reliable, but he did lose a fumble during this game. This was the first time this season that Penix threw multiple touchdowns in a game. He hasn't been a great fantasy option so far this season, but this performance should give fantasy managers some hope. We'll see what he can put together against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7.

items.h: Michael Penix Jr. tosses three touchdowns in Week 6 loss to Bears
items.s: Michael Penix Jr. completed 19-of-33 pass attempts for 225 yards and three touchdowns while rushing once for one yard and losing a fumble in the Falcons' 31-23 Week 6 loss to the Chicago Bears. Penix Jr. has been mostly reliable behind center in his return to the lineup, throwing for one or more touchdowns in each of his last three contests. The quarterback remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 7 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

items.h: Penix (ribs) practiced without limitations again Thursday, Daniel Flick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
items.s: Penix has faced no limitations in Atlanta's first two practices ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears, suggesting that he's good to go after subbing out late in this past Sunday's overtime loss to the Ravens, in which Tua Tagovailoa threw the game-losing interception in OT. The Falcons have scored 34.3 points per game in Penix's three starts after averaging 8.0 PPG in the first two games of the season while Penix was wrapping up the rehab on his torn ACL.

items.h: Penix (ribs) was a full practice participant Wednesday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.s: Penix suffered a rib injury late in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's loss to the Ravens, which didn't allow him to take the field for the Falcons' only possession of overtime. Head coach Kevin Stefanski told Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com that Penix was slated to be limited at Wednesday's practice, but afterward the quarterback himself relayed to Josh Kendall of The Athletic that he "made every throw out there" and is "good to go this week." Penix's subsequent full listing indicates as much, and he'll remain Atlanta's starting quarterback for Sunday's contest against the Bears.

items.s: Penix was injured after taking a big hit on Atlanta's final possession of the fourth quarter. He came back into the game after missing one play and threw an incomplete pass to close out regulation before being listed as questionable to return for the extra period. He ultimately remained on the bench for overtime, with backup Tua Tagovailoa stepping in for Penix and throwing a game-ending interception on Atlanta's second offensive play of the extra session. The oft-injured Penix will try to overcome this latest setback before the Falcons host the Bears next Sunday.
